note: Agent tier, two cli rules, each judged against the agent's fix marked addressed (n-0510, n-0511) and against its statement. Driven with node bin/walkdown.js from the working tree (693d955-dirty) on fresh mktemp HOMEs with WALKDOWN_HOME=$HOME/.walkdown and real git repos; the pre-ADR-0014 machine was made with main's own old CLI (git archive 8bcc2ca), not by hand. results.reasoning: I judged this against n-0510, whose fix has the RSpec formatter read identity.username from profile.yml and then from config.yml. On a machine set up by `walkdown init` and `blueprints new`, I ran real rspec with -I adapters/rspec/lib -r walkdown/formatter --format Walkdown::Formatter, bare and through `walkdown run`, beside the node:test and Playwright reporters through `walkdown run`. With profile.yml naming topher-x and git naming ghpat, all four runs were recorded under topher-x, so the fix holds on an upgraded machine. Before an upgrade, with only the config.yml old walkdown wrote, `walkdown run` refuses with exit 2. Bare rspec now records topher-x, but bare node:test and Playwright record ghpat, because lib/identity.js reads only profile.yml. The reply on n-0510 says the formatter reads config.yml 'as the CLI does', and the CLI never does. With no profile.yml at all, which is what `blueprints new` leaves on a machine that never ran `init`, the formatter skips git and records Etc.getlogin. Under this harness that is 'root', though the user is topherfangio, while the node:test and Playwright runs record ghpat. 'root' is not among the handles defaultActor offers (ghpat, topherfangio, Pat Example), so that run reads as somebody else. Both cases are machines walkdown itself made, and in each one person's runs go under two usernames, one of them nobody's. That breaks 'every record is written under the username of the person who made it' and the steps' 'personal config, or failing that git'. The run-under-username screen is fine: it shows actor and signer as sam, never the full name.

I judged this against n-0511, which makes a row's formerly: ID resolve anywhere and adds `walkdown upgrade --code`. The old machine held hireart_main and shop as personal homes and app as a committed home, each with a passing run and an n-000x thread. `status` said an upgrade was due, named the command, exited 2 and changed nothing, checked by a hash of every file. The codes a, abcd, a-b, 'h a' and ÄB were each refused before anything moved. `upgrade --code ha` in ~/hireart gave 0001-ha-hireart-main with formerly: hireart_main. config.yml became profile.yml, homes were flattened and got records.yml, personal homes moved under projects/<label>/ keeping their folder names, and threads got UUIDs and kept their labels. Status showed every verdict as before, and a second run said nothing to do. hireart_main, shop and app resolved from / for where, status and a threads write, each with the 'was called before' reason. A --commit spec home lost the shared .gitignore and got its own. Two defects break the rule, though. First, a taken code is refused only inside the registry step. `upgrade --code hr` in ~/shop moved the profile, flattened all three homes, removed ~/shop/.walkdown/config.yml, rewrote CLAUDE.md and moved hireart's home to projects/hireart/. It then refused, leaving the registry naming the old path. Every later `walkdown upgrade` fails with 'already exists ... was not moved', so the machine is half-moved, which is what the rule is there to prevent, and it cannot be recovered with walkdown. Second, a formerly ID is checked before a name in the project you stand in. In a new project ~/other whose blueprint is named shop, `--blueprint shop` resolved to ~/shop's 0002-sp-shop, and `sweep --blueprint shop` wrote a sweep into the wrong project, staling its verdicts. As minor points, `--code ' '`, or a --code given outside any registered project, is dropped without a word. The upgrade screen reads plainly.
